Transcripts underwent deductive analysis using the Donabedian quality framework and inductive thematic analysis using an adapted socioecological model.

**RESULTS**: Twenty-six clinicians from 23 trauma centers participated; 22 (85%) were surgeons, 25 (96%) practiced at Level I trauma centers, and 24 (92%) worked in academic hospitals. Participants identified 7 geriatric-centered structures, 21 care processes, and 11 outcomes considered important for assessing geriatric trauma care. Four themes emerged: variation in geriatric care structures and pathways across hospitals; financial, staffing, and organizational constraints; evolving professional identity and ownership of geriatric trauma care; and gaps in measuring outcomes important to older adults. Although clinicians described implementing selected components of national guidelines, no common comprehensive care model emerged. Participants emphasized that conventional hospital-based metrics inadequately capture postdischarge recovery, particularly functional status, independence, and quality of life.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Trauma clinicians reported substantial variation in geriatric-centered care, shaped by institutional resources, organizational priorities, and professional culture. Limited measurement of patient-centered, longitudinal outcomes constrains evaluation of geriatric trauma care. Incorporating functional recovery and quality of life into trauma quality assessment may help identify effective care structures and processes.

articles.title: A Novel Surgical Technique for Post-traumatic Syringomyelia Progressing to the Medulla Oblongata: Evidence of Upward Drainage of Central Canal Fluid Within the Spinal Cord: Corrigendum.
Endotracheal intubation practices, success rates and adverse events in four Dutch emergency departments: a multicentre retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Endotracheal intubation in the emergency department (ED) is a high-risk intervention associated with significant complications. Contemporary European data on emergency airway management remain limited, and no published data are available from the Netherlands. This study aimed to describe endotracheal intubation practices, success rates, and adverse events in four Dutch EDs.

**METHODS**: We conducted a multicentre retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing endotracheal intubation in four teaching hospital EDs in the Netherlands between January 2019 and December 2023. Patients were identified using procedure registrations, diagnostic codes, billing information and disposition records. Trained abstractors collected standardized data on patient characteristics, indications, provider characteristics, intubation techniques, medications, first-pass success and adverse events.

**RESULTS**: A total of 1250 intubations were included. The most common indication was post-return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) after cardiac arrest (47%), followed by neurologic pathology (14%), cardiac arrest (12%), respiratory insufficiency (8%), intoxication (8%), and trauma (5%). Emergency medicine and intensive care physicians performed most intubations. Videolaryngoscopy was the primary technique in 89.5% of cases, and etomidate was the most frequently used induction agent (73.5%). The overall first-pass success rate was 93.8% and did not differ by provider specialty or level of training. Adverse events occurred in 181 patients (14.5%), with hypotension (6.5%) and desaturation (4.7%) being most common. Increasing age (OR 1.07 per year, 95% CI 1.04-1.10) and cardiac pathology as indication for intubation (OR 3.50, 95% CI 1.03-11.88) were associated with hypotension. A higher body mass index (OR 1.08 per point, 95% CI 1.03-1.13), younger age (OR 0.98 per year, 95% CI 0.96-1.00, p = 0.022) and multiple intubations attempts (OR 2.9, 95% CI 1.12-7.33) were associated with desaturation. Lower pre-intubation oxygen saturation was associated with peri-intubation cardiac arrest (OR 0.96 per point, 95% CI 0.92-0.99).

**CONCLUSIONS**: This study provides the first multicentre description of emergency airway management in Dutch EDs and demonstrates a distinctive emergency intubation population, characterised by a high proportion of post-ROSC intubations. Contemporary practice was characterised by widespread adoption of videolaryngoscopy, frequent use of etomidate, and high first-pass success rates. Peri-intubation hypotension and desaturation remained common and represent important targets for quality improvement.

**TRIAL REGISTRATION**: clinicaltrials.gov NCT06374030.
articles.journal: Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med

articles.title: Predicting mortality in pediatric cases with severe traumatic brain injury: is the Eppendorf-Cologne Scale more reliable than Glasgow Coma Scale?
articles.abstract:
**PURPOSE**: Severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) in children is a major cause of morbidity and mortality, requiring reliable tools for early assessment and prognosis. While the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) is the standard neurological evaluation tool, it has limitations in pediatric patients. The Eppendorf-Cologne Scale (ECS), originally developed for adults, emphasizes pupil size, reactivity, and motor response and may offer advantages in children.

**METHODS**: This multicenter cohort study analyzed TraumaRegister DGU

**RESULTS**: Among the cohort, 2,582 patients (44.1%) had severe TBI and 476 (8.1%) died in hospital. GCS showed slightly higher accuracy for predicting severe TBI (AUROC 0.778, 95% CI 0.766-0.791) than ECS (AUROC 0.745, 95% CI 0.731-0.758). For mortality prediction, ECS performed marginally better (AUROC 0.943, 95% CI 0.929-0.957) than GCS (AUROC 0.910, 95% CI 0.896-0.924). Mortality rates were 90% in the worst ECS category and 55% in the worst GCS category.

**CONCLUSION**: GCS showed higher discrimination for severe TBI, whereas ECS showed higher discrimination for in-hospital mortality among patients with severe TBI. ECS may provide complementary prognostic information, but its clinical utility and role alongside GCS require prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Blunt anatomical cardiac injury (BACI) - lessons from a single trauma center cohort.
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: Patients with anatomical damage to the heart after blunt trauma are rarely seen in hospital settings due to their elevated prehospital mortality. The aim of this study is to review our center experience with this entity.

**METHODS**: After institutional research board approval, a local Trauma Databank search (Qatar National Trauma Registry) was performed from 2016 to 2025. Cases presented with blunt trauma and anatomical changes to pericardium or heart, detected in imaging or surgery, in patients above 13 years old were diagnosed as blunt anatomical cardiac injury - BACI and included.

**RESULTS**: Amongst 17542 blunt trauma cases admitted to our Trauma Center during the study period, 15 patients (0.09% incidence) met the inclusion/exclusion criteria. All patients were males, with average age of 43 years (ranges 26-75), with ISS of 32 (ranges 10-75). The most common mechanism of injury was pedestrian struck (5cases -33%). Hypotension at trauma room assessment was common (8 cases - 53% of patients) and 8 patients (53%) required surgery. FAST, echocardiogram and computed tomography were used as diagnostic tools. The patients presented in 4 anatomical patterns: (a) intracardiac/valve damage; (b) pericardial effusion; (c) pericardial laceration and (d) cardiac rupture. Three patients (20%) died, all during emergent surgery and sustaining cardiac rupture.

**CONCLUSION**: BACI is uncommonly seen at Emergency Departments and carries elevated early mortality in cases with cardiac rupture, requiring high index of suspicion for diagnosis. Different clinical presentations of BACI were observed and described in this series. Further studies with larger number of patients are needed to further clarify possible differences in severity, surgical requirement and mortality according to the BACI structural presentation.

articles.title: Management of Traumatic Pneumothorax in the Emergency Department: A Two-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVE**: To describe clinical characteristics, initial emergency department (ED) management strategy (conservative or chest drain) and outcomes of patients who present to the ED with traumatic pneumothorax.

**METHODS**: Retrospective cohort study of patients aged 14 years and older with an ED diagnosis of traumatic pneumothorax between January 2023 and March 2025 in two EDs. Pleural intervention was defined as needle decompression, thoracostomy, or chest drain. Descriptive data are reported, and logistic regression was used to identify predictors of ED-initiated chest drain insertion.

**RESULTS**: Of 339 eligible patients, 50 had a pre-hospital pleural intervention, of which 27 had chest drains inserted to formalise (finger) thoracostomy or needle decompression. A further 58 patients received an ED-initiated chest drain, for a total of 85 ED chest drains (25.1%). Of the 231 (68.1%) who were initially managed conservatively, 53 received a drain during their hospital stay, primarily as part of surgical management. The majority (71.9%) of drains were large-bore (≥ 24 Fr). Predictors of ED-initiated pleural drainage were: pneumothorax size > 35 mm (aOR 41.0, 95% CI 16.4-102) and presence of haemothorax (aOR 6.3, 95% CI 2.5-15.8). Thirty-six drained patients (22.8%) had a recorded complication. In-hospital mortality was 5.6%.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Two-thirds of patients with traumatic pneumothorax were initially managed without drainage before departing the ED. Later drainage frequently reflected operative or broader trauma management rather than clinical deterioration. Pneumothorax size and haemothorax were independent factors associated with ED-initiated drainage. The predominance of large-bore drains and frequency of complications identify opportunities for structured selective management and drain-selection pathways.

articles.title: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome.
articles.abstract: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a common cause of acute hypoxemic respiratory failure in patients with pneumonia, sepsis, aspiration of gastric contents, severe trauma, or other inciting triggers. Although the definition of the syndrome has evolved over the past several decades, the core elements (acute onset, hypoxemia, and bilateral radiographic opacities) remain consistent. Critical components of management include identification and treatment of the underlying cause of ARDS as well as avoidance of ventilator-induced lung injury and volume overload. Ongoing areas of controversy include the best strategy for supporting nonintubated patients, personalization of positive end-expiratory pressure, the role of innovative ventilatory strategies, and the use of glucocorticoids. New research suggests that precision medicine approaches to ARDS management that focus on discrete biologic, radiographic, or physiological subphenotypes may improve outcomes, and prospective trials of these approaches are ongoing.

articles.title: Hospital-Based Violence Intervention and Fragmentation of Trauma Care.
ICU Mortality Associated With Clinically Important Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding: A Multistate Analysis.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: Clinically important upper gastrointestinal bleeding may increase mortality and time to discharge from the ICU. Conventional analyses ignore timing and treat bleeding as a binary event. We evaluated the association between time-dependent clinically important upper gastrointestinal bleeding and ICU mortality.

**DESIGN AND SETTING**: A multicenter cohort study using data from an international stress ulcer prophylaxis trial.

**PATIENTS**: A total of 4821 invasively ventilated adult participants.

**INTERVENTIONS**: None.

**MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS**: A multistate model was specified with two transient ICU states (bleed-free and post-bleed) and four absorbing states (ICU discharge or death, each with or without bleeding). The Aalen-Johansen method was used to estimate transition and state occupancy probabilities and to describe risks of different clinical courses. Follow-up was censored at 90 days. We fit two Cox models for time to death in the ICU regressing on time-dependent bleeding history while adjusting for age, sex, baseline Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II score, admission category (medical/surgical/trauma), vasopressor/inotrope use and renal replacement therapy on study day 1 and randomized allocation of pantoprazole or placebo; a second model also adjusted for time-dependent covariates of advanced life support (invasive mechanical ventilation, vasopressor/inotrope use, and renal replacement therapy). Clinically important upper gastrointestinal bleeding developed in 104 patients (2.2%) in the ICU. Median ICU length of stay for those who experienced bleeding was 19 days (interquartile range [IQR], 11-30 d) vs. 9 days (IQR, 5-15 d) for those who did not. Accounting for immortal time bias, the time-dependent indicator of clinically important upper gastrointestinal bleeding was associated with increased ICU mortality (hazard ratio, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.13-2.15). At any time, patients who experienced bleeding had approximately 1.6 times the hazard of ICU mortality compared with those without a history of bleeding.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Clinically important upper gastrointestinal bleeding as a time-dependent event is associated with an increased risk of ICU mortality.

articles.title: Propranolol administration following traumatic brain injury induces distinct neuroinflammatory gene expression profiles.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains a major cause of morbidity and is frequently followed by prolonged intensive care stays with sustained physiologic stress. Beta-blockade has been investigated as an adjunct therapy for TBI given its potential to reduce sympathetic hyperactivation. The molecular mechanisms underlying neuroinflammatory signaling remain incompletely defined. We hypothesized that propranolol (BB) administration following TBI would modify neuroinflammatory transcriptional responses consistent with attenuation of maladaptive inflammatory signaling.

**METHODS**: Male Sprague-Dawley rats (n=6-8/group) were divided into 6 groups: (1) TBI7d (controlled cortical impact) followed by 7 days of daily handling, (2) TBI7d with daily propranolol administration (TBI BB7d), (3) TBI with chronic restraint stress for 7 days (TBI CRS7d), (4) TBI CRS7d with daily propranolol administration (TBI CRS BB7d), (5) CRS7d (n=7) who underwent daily stress exposure for 7 days; and (6) CRS BB7d (n=7) underwent daily stress exposure with propranolol injections for 7 days. RNA was extracted from the injured frontal lobe and analyzed using the NanoString Neuroinflammation panel. Differential gene expression was analyzed using ROSALIND. Significant differentially expressed genes (sDEGs) were defined as fold change ≥1.5 or ≤-1.5 with p<0.05. Functional pathway analysis was performed using Qiagen Ingenuity Pathway Analysis.

**RESULTS**: Compared with TBI alone, TBI BB7d demonstrated 83 sDEGs, including genes associated with neuronal signaling, neurotransmitter regulation, and epigenetic modulation. Pathway analysis identified significant involvement of the IL8 signaling and FXR/RXR. In the TBI CRS7d model, propranolol treatment yielded 21 sDEGs. These genes were enriched in pathways related to cellular stress responses and inflammatory regulation. Propranolol downregulated IL6, IL8, and neuroinflammation signaling pathways.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Propranolol administration following TBI, with and without stress, resulted in distinct neuroinflammatory transcriptional profiles. Propranolol was associated with alterations in multiple pathways involved in stress response, immune regulation, and neurorecovery. These findings suggest beta-blockade may modulate stress-related neuroinflammatory signaling following TBI.

articles.title: The Radiographic Lung Edema Score in Pediatric Acute Respiratory Failure: Associations With Systemic Inflammatory Biomarkers and Multiple Organ Dysfunction.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: Although chest radiographs (CXR) are among the most used imaging modalities in critically ill patients, their interpretation and clinical significance remain incompletely leveraged. The Radiographic Lung Edema (RALE) score is a prognostic bedside tool widely applied in adults to quantify lung edema on CXR. However, this score has been infrequently studied in children, and its potential to reflect broader aspects of critical illness pathophysiology beyond the lungs is unknown. We sought to determine the reproducibility of the RALE score, and whether higher RALE scores were associated with circulating inflammatory and endothelial biomarkers, multi-organ dysfunction, and worse clinical outcomes in pediatric acute respiratory failure (ARF).

**DESIGN**: Retrospective cohort study.

**SETTING**: Multicenter PICUs.

**PATIENTS**: Critically ill children (2 wk to 17 yr old) receiving invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) for ARF, enrolled in the CAF-PINT (Coagulation and Fibrinolysis in Pediatric Insulin Titration) study (2012-2016).

**INTERVENTIONS**: None.

**MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS**: A baseline RALE score was calculated for each patient from a single CXR obtained within 72 hours of IMV initiation. Among 212 patients, RALE scores demonstrated good inter-rater reliability (intra-class coefficient 0.85; 95% CI, 0.82-0.87). After adjustment for ARF etiology and illness severity, higher RALE scores were associated with fewer 28-day ventilator-free days (sub-distribution hazard ratio per 1-sd increase, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.69-0.95). Structural equation modeling demonstrated that this association was mediated through both pulmonary dysfunction, measured by the oxygenation index (β -0.14; 95% bootstrapped CI, -0.22 to -0.06), and extrapulmonary organ dysfunction, measured by the Pediatric Logistic Organ Dysfunction score (β -0.05; 95% bootstrapped CI, -0.10 to -0.002). Similar associations were observed for 28-day PICU-free days. Finally, penalized regression selected soluble triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells-1, intercellular adhesion molecule-1, and tumor necrosis factor receptor-1 as biomarkers associated with higher RALE scores.

**CONCLUSIONS**: We provide evidence that the RALE score is not solely a lung injury marker but also reflects broader systemic pathophysiology. These findings have important implications for the interpretation and clinical application of this bedside tool in pediatric ARF.

articles.title: State Variation in Crime Victim Compensation Denials after Violent Injury in the United States.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Crime victim compensation (CVC) can offset financial burdens after violent injury, yet state-level administrative requirements may restrict access. We examined variation in CVC denials and associations with modifiable program policies.

**STUDY DESIGN**: This cross-sectional study analyzed Office for Victims of Crime administrative data from all 50 states and Washington, D.C., for fiscal year 2023. State program characteristics and socioeconomic vulnerability were evaluated against application denial rates using multivariable beta regression. Hierarchical clustering identified denial-reason profiles; leave-one-state-out analyses assessed robustness.

**RESULTS**: Across 51 programs, denial rates ranged from 3.9% to 75% (median 25%; IQR, 14%-39%). States permitting exemptions from law enforcement reporting had lower denial rates than states requiring reporting (OR 0.56; 95% CI, 0.34-0.93; p=0.024). Higher state-level socioeconomic vulnerability was associated with higher denial rates (OR 5.5; 95% CI, 1.5-20; p=0.009). Incomplete information (26%) and ineligible applications (24%) were the leading denial reasons. The administrative-barrier cluster encompassed 27 states and had the highest mean denial rate (34.4%), compared with 17.1% in the behavioral-scrutiny cluster (p=0.04 for pairwise comparison). Reporting-exemption associations retained their direction across all 51 leave-one-state-out models and remained statistically significant in 50.

**CONCLUSIONS**: CVC denial rates vary markedly across states and are associated with law enforcement reporting policies and socioeconomic vulnerability. Administrative documentation barriers characterize states with higher denial rates. Expanding reporting exemptions and integrating application navigation into trauma care warrant evaluation as strategies to improve access to post-injury financial assistance.

articles.title: Shift change: 12- versus 24-hour work period models in acute care surgery.
Nursing led protocols in trauma: a point-counterpoint analysis.
articles.abstract: This narrative point-counterpoint analysis examines the benefits, risks, and implementation requirements of nursing-led medication administration protocols in trauma and emergency care. It draws on the debate at the 2026 Maryland Committee on Trauma Point/Counterpoint XLIII Conference in Baltimore and selected published literature to develop practical recommendations for clinical use and evaluation. The conference proposition that these protocols save lives is examined critically; this article does not report an original outcomes study. Reported benefits include earlier medication administration, improved symptom management, and more consistent delivery of indicated treatment. One randomized emergency department evaluation reported a 186-min reduction in median time to acetaminophen, and a retrospective intracerebral hemorrhage cohort associated nursing-led protocol changes with faster blood pressure control. These findings support improvements in care processes but do not establish a general survival benefit in trauma. Risks include inappropriate patient selection, medication errors, delayed escalation, and excessive protocol complexity. Safe implementation requires multidisciplinary agreement on scope, clear eligibility and exclusion criteria, accessible escalation pathways, and education that accounts for staff turnover and fatigue. Protocols should be integrated into trauma and emergency performance improvement processes to monitor adherence, treatment timeliness, adverse events, and patient outcomes, with feedback and reassessment after corrective action. Nursing-led medication protocols can improve timely care when supported by these safeguards; their effectiveness and sustainability require ongoing evaluation in the populations and settings where they are used.

articles.title: Should MAP augmentation remain the standard therapy after traumatic spinal cord injury?
articles.abstract: Traumatic spinal cord injury (SCI) remains one of the most devastating injuries in trauma care. For nearly three decades, maintenance of elevated mean arterial pressure (MAP) has been advocated to mitigate secondary ischemic injury after SCI and help preserve or improve neurologic outcomes. Although current guidelines continue to recommend augmentation of MAP and strict avoidance of hypotension, the supporting evidence remains predominantly observational. At the 41st Annual Point/counterpoint Acute Care Surgery Conference, experts debated whether MAP augmentation remains necessary after SCI. This review summarizes the physiologic rationale, supporting and opposing clinical evidence, emerging concepts in spinal cord perfusion pressure, and future directions in hemodynamic management. Level of evidence: III.

articles.title: Early Prehospital Prediction of Neurological Outcome After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Derivation and External Validation of the MIRA-29 Score.
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: Out-of-hospital cardiac (OHCA) arrest is a frequent emergency, and few patients will survive with good neurological outcome. Identification of patients with a low likelihood of meaningful recovery represents a major clinical challenge. Numerous scores have been developed to guide decision-making after OHCA, with variable goals and targets, but most of them have been validated on small cohorts, integrates variables not available in the prehospital field, or do have low prediction values. MIRA-29 score aimed to only rely on simple clinical variables, available in the prehospital setting. We hypothetized that such score will provide incremental neurological prognosis value at an early-stage following OHCA.

**METHODS**: MIRA-29 score was derived and internally validated over a five-year period on a prospective cohort of 1099 adult patients, including all OHCA treated by our territory dispatch center. Multivariate analysis identified independent variables within the database, that were used to optimize the prediction model using machine-learning and genetic algorithms. The score was subsequently validated externally on 82 696 patients extracted from the French national cardiac arrest registry (RéAC).

**RESULTS**: Out from the 1099 patients, 85 patients (7.7%) had a favorable neurological outcome. Multivariate analysis identified five independent variables associated with neurological outcome: age, low-flow duration, number of external electric shock, epinephrine dose, and the OHCA site (street, public facility, home). After model optimization and machine-learning, age was not retained within the final model. External validation depicted a precision of 0.86 and a recall of 0.88 of the model. The F1-Score and accuracy are respectively 0.87 and 0.88, and specificity for a bad neurological prognosis is 0.99.

**CONCLUSION**: MIRA‑29 strength lies on its ability to reliably identify patients with extremely high probability of poor neurological outcome, while being based on four simple clinical variables. The prospective validation of MIRA-29 in the clinical setting may evaluate its impact on clinical decision making.

articles.title: RescQ™: One-year implementation and feasibility results of a digitally enabled support pathway for bystanders of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Bystanders to out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) are at significant risk of psychological distress, yet no standardised support pathway exists for them in the UK. RescQ™ is a digital-first bystander support pathway embedded within regional prehospital and cardiac arrest care services.

**AIM**: To evaluate the feasibility of embedding RescQ™ into routine emergency medical services (EMS) practice leading to appropriate contact with bystanders involved in OHCA. Secondary aims were to describe digital access, demand for liaison officer (LO) support, identification of younger bystanders, and EMS clinician acceptability.

**METHODS**: Prospective one-year regional service evaluation of RescQ™ across Essex, UK. Bystanders involved in eligible OHCA events were registered by EMS clinicians and provided with immediate access to secure digital resources. Bystanders could self-refer for additional support through LO.

**RESULTS**: During the one-year evaluation, 220 of 432 eligible OHCA incidents had at least one bystander identified and the incident entered into the RescQ™ pathway, representing an incident-level capture rate of 50.9%. Across these incidents, 298 bystanders were identified, of whom 260 eligible adults were registered with RescQ™. Of registered adult bystanders, 96.2% accessed the digital resources at least once. Among all identified bystanders, 30/298 (10.1%) were aged under 18 years. Approximately 10% of registered bystanders self-referred for additional personalised LO support. Among 25 EMS clinician survey respondents who had used RescQ™ in clinical practice, ratings indicated acceptability.

**CONCLUSION**: RescQ™ demonstrated the feasibility of identifying and supporting bystanders following OHCA through a digitally enabled pathway, achieving incident-level capture above the pre-specified feasibility threshold and high website access among registered adults. These findings support further multi-region evaluation of implementation, sustainability and scalability across different EMS systems.

articles.title: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrests due to foreign body airway obstruction: A CanROC registry, retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Foreign body airway obstruction (FBAO) is a treatable cause of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), but North American data are limited.

**METHODS**: Exploratory retrospective cohort study of EMS-treated OHCAs using the Canadian Resuscitation Outcomes Consortium (CanROC) registry (2005-2023), classified as obviously FBAO-related or of no obvious cause (presumed cardiac). Logistic regression compared Utstein characteristics between etiologies and identified factors associated with prehospital return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) and survival to acute care discharge.

**RESULTS**: Among 105,178 EMS-treated OHCAs, 1,106(1.1%) were obviously FBAO-related. Compared with cases of no obvious cause, obviously FBAO-related cases were older (median 73 vs 68 years, p<0.001), more often witnessed (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.98[5.36-9.25]), more often attended by trained bystanders (aOR 3.30[2.41-4.41]), and less often had a shockable rhythm (aOR 0.11[0.07-0.15]). Obviously FBAO-related cases more often achieved prehospital ROSC (62.7% vs 37.8%; OR 2.77[2.44-3.13]), but survival did not differ (10.6% vs 9.0%,p=0.094). Within the obviously FBAO-related cohort, ROSC was associated with witnessed arrest (aOR 1.66[1.13-2.43]) and shorter EMS response time (aOR 0.95 per minute[0.92-0.99]). Survival was associated with younger age (aOR 0.76 per decade[0.61-0.93]), initial shockable rhythm (aOR 4.76[1.55-13.30]), and shorter EMS response time (aOR 0.81 per minute[0.66-0.98]). Survival was 18.1% and 0.8% among obviously FBAO-related OHCAs with and without prehospital ROSC, respectively.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Obviously FBAO-related OHCAs are uncommon but clinically distinct. ROSC is frequent, yet survival remains low and is associated with early prehospital factors, supporting choking prevention initiatives, bystander training, and rapid EMS response.

articles.title: Field Amputation by helicopter emergency service personnel: A cross-sectional survey of clinical practice and experience within air ambulance services in England.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Field Amputation (FA) is a rare, but potentially life-saving procedure undertaken by helicopter emergency medical services (HEMS) in the UK. Literature pertaining to FA predominantly originates from outside the UK, where the operational, clinical and legal differences make its applicability to the UK uncertain. Consequently, the severe lack of FA reports from the UK mean that FA is poorly documented in this setting. The aim is to establish the current prehospital FA clinical guidance and practice in the UK.

**METHOD/DISCUSSION**: An electronic, cross-sectional survey was sent to all UK HEMS. The survey sought to improve understanding of clinical practice, including service provision, scope of practice, equipment, training, governance and incidences of FA. Surveys were analysed with descriptive statistics and descriptive thematic analysis.

**RESULTS**: 15 HEMS responded, with 14 included for final analysis after one response was excluded. All respondents were from England. Every HEMS (n = 14, 100%) could provide FA, with 12 (86%) having a Clinical Practice Guideline specific to FA. Four services (29%) had undertaken FA within the last five years, totalling six cases, which were deemed notable given the absence of case reports from the UK in that time. A Gigli saw was the most popular instrument for bone disarticulation (n = 13, 93%). Unlike the USA and Korea, no respondents used hospital response teams to provide FA.

**CONCLUSION**: FA service provision is widely available across England, with cases of FA being undertaken, yet little standardisation nationally. A national or international registry of every FA case could provide further insights into this area of clinical practice.

articles.title: The epidemiology and burden of injury in The Gambia: A prospective trauma registry study.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Traumatic injury is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet robust prospective data characterizing injury epidemiology remain limited across sub-Saharan Africa. This study describes the demographic, injury, and initial treatment characteristics of patients enrolled in a hospital-based trauma registry in The Gambia. These data provide a foundation for characterizing the country's injury burden, guiding resource allocation, and informing continued trauma-system development.

**METHODS**: A prospective descriptive study was conducted using data from a hospital-based trauma registry established at Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital, The Gambia's principal tertiary referral center for trauma and orthopaedic care. Injured patients presenting to the Trauma Emergency Unit from June 2022 through September 2025 were enrolled. Data included demographics, injury mechanism and setting, intent, anatomic injury location, injury type, and Trauma Emergency Unit disposition. Descriptive statistics were calculated.

**RESULTS**: Of 3380 enrolled patients, 76.1% were male, with a median age of 25 years. Most injuries occurred in villages (41.1%). Transport-related injuries were the leading mechanism (47.1%), followed by falls (29.3%) and violence/assault (21.4%). Streets/highways were the most common place of injury (43.3%), and nearly all injuries were unintentional (96.1%). The lower extremity below the knee (29.6%), head (22.3%), and hand (21.7%) were the most frequently injured body regions. Soft tissue injuries predominated (57.0%), followed by closed fractures (24.3%) and open fractures (11.7%). Overall, 55.9% of patients were discharged home, 29.3% were dispositioned to the operating theatre, and 10.1% left without being seen or before completing treatment. Among patients with recorded Trauma Emergency Unit disposition, 2.6% (n = 84) were categorized as 'mortuary or died.'

**CONCLUSIONS**: To our knowledge, this represents the largest prospective trauma registry analysis of injury epidemiology in The Gambia. Trauma disproportionately affected young males and was driven primarily by transport-related injuries, with a substantial burden occurring in rural settings. The frequency of fractures and incomplete treatment encounters highlights priorities for road-safety interventions, strengthened prehospital and referral systems, and expanded trauma, orthopaedic, and diagnostic capacity. Continued prospective trauma surveillance can support resource allocation, quality improvement, and national trauma-system development.

articles.title: Exposure technology and tissue protection in anterior and anterolateral thoracic/thoracolumbar fracture surgery: An international surgeon survey of retractor performance, mitigation strategies, and design priorities.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Anterior and anterolateral thoracic/thoracolumbar fracture surgery can provide direct vertebral-body and ventral canal access but requires controlled exposure through deep, anatomy-constrained corridors. We evaluated surgeon-reported retractor performance, tissue-protection behaviors, and device-design priorities.

**METHODS**: An international web-based survey was completed by 82 surgeons from 22 countries. Detailed analyses were restricted to 39 surgeons who reported personal anterior/anterolateral T4-L2 fracture surgery within 5 years. Likert items, multi-select mitigation strategies, and 26 free-text design responses were summarized descriptively; Rasch hierarchy, specialty differential item functioning (DIF), and MADQ3 residual correlations were exploratory response-structure analyses.

**RESULTS**: Standard rib spreaders, table-mounted ring retractors, and expandable lateral retractors were each used by 17/39 surgeons (43.6%). Prominent signals were large body habitus increasing difficulty and pressure (28/33, 84.8%), adjunct visualization (28/35, 80.0%), T11-L2 working distance (27/34, 79.4%), stability/minimal creep (26/37, 70.3%), and blade geometry (21/31, 67.7%). Common protective strategies were avoiding the inferior-rib neurovascular bundle (23/39, 59.0%), periodic partial release (20/39, 51.3%), and limiting blade opening according to imaging or chest-wall size (15/39, 38.5%). Overall soft-tissue risk (7/36, 19.4%) and reported complication frequency (1/33, 3.0%) had lower upper-category endorsement. Design responses prioritized blade geometry/pressure distribution (13/26, 50.0%), integrated illumination (12/26, 46.2%), and imaging/optical integration (11/26, 42.3%). No DIF signal survived false-discovery-rate correction.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Surgeons conceptualized safe exposure as a coupled mechanical, visual, and tissue-loading problem. Future retractor systems should be evaluated at depth for stability, pressure distribution, blade geometry, illumination, imaging compatibility, and workflow using objective bench and cadaveric metrics.

articles.title: Retrograde gearshift pedicle probe-assisted reduction of displaced superior pubic rami fractures: A technical note.
articles.abstract: Percutaneous fixation of superior pubic ramus fractures relies on establishment of safe corridors. Rotational and multiplanar deformity due to fracture disrupts the corridors and percutaneous or open reduction of these fractures is challenging. Retrograde insertion of a curved gearshift pedicle probe allows the surgeon to create a joystick to affect translation, rotation and angulation with a single instrument to restore the superior pubic ramus corridor and allow passage of an antegrade wire or screw. Following corridor restoration, reduction was captured antegrade, while definitive implant type and trajectory were selected independently according to fracture and osseous corridor morphology. Three displaced superior pubic ramus fractures were treated using this technique including mid-ramus, high ramus and segmental fractures with translational and rotational components. The probe was effectively used to de-rotate and reduce the fractures to allow for safe insertion of internal fixation with full containment and no complications. The curved gearshift pedicle probe is a rigid intramedullary reduction aid capable of multiplanar fragment manipulation and restoration of superior pubic ramus corridor while preserving independent selection of definitive fixation.

articles.title: Concomitant pelvic ring injury compromises acetabular reduction quality: A propensity score-matched analysis with surgical sequence subgroup study.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Concomitant pelvic ring injury is reported to compromise acetabular fracture reduction, yet matched comparisons are scarce and the optimal surgical sequence remains debated. We assessed whether pelvic ring injury compromises anatomical acetabular reduction, and whether fixation sequence influences reduction quality and complications.

**METHODS**: We retrospectively reviewed 119 consecutive patients with isolated displaced acetabular fractures and 20 patients with combined pelvic ring and acetabular injuries treated at a tertiary trauma center (2004-2023). One-to-one propensity score matching using age, sex, and Letournel classification yielded 20 matched pairs (n = 40). Within the combined group, eight patients underwent acetabulum-first and 12 underwent pelvic ring-first fixation. The primary outcome was anatomical acetabular reduction (modified Matta criteria, 0-1 mm) graded by two independent reviewers. Secondary outcomes were pelvic ring reduction and postoperative complications.

**RESULTS**: Anatomical acetabular reduction was achieved in 14 of 20 isolated patients (70.0%) versus four of 20 combined patients (20.0%; p = 0.004). Within combined injuries, acetabulum-first showed a numerical trend toward better reduction (37.5% vs 8.3% anatomical; p = 0.132). Pelvic ring reduction did not differ between sequence subgroups (75.0% vs 83.3%; p = 0.450). Excluding pre-existing sciatic palsies, any complication occurred in two of eight acetabulum-first (25.0%) versus eight of 12 pelvic ring-first patients (66.7%; p = 0.170), driven by post-traumatic osteoarthritis (12.5% vs 41.7%).

**CONCLUSION**: Concomitant pelvic ring injury significantly compromises anatomical acetabular reduction. Where precise pelvic ring reduction is achievable, pelvic ring-first fixation remains appropriate; where it is not, acetabulum-first or temporary pelvic stabilization followed by definitive fixation should be considered to avoid fixing the acetabulum onto a malreduced pelvic ring.

articles.title: A Mobile Application Improves Paramedic Performance in Simulated Trauma Care: A Crossover Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: Clinical performance during prehospital trauma care varies among emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians, particularly during high-stress critical responses. We developed a mobile application providing real-time access to local treatment protocols, decision support tools, and instructional procedure videos to supplement standard practice. We evaluated whether use of the application improved paramedic performance during simulated trauma scenarios.

**METHODS**: We conducted a crossover randomized controlled trial between July 2025 and February 2026 comparing standard care alone with standard care plus the mobile application during two high-fidelity trauma simulations (one adult and one pediatric). Paramedics, working in pairs, were block randomized to one of four sequences, varying both the scenario order and the application use. Performance was assessed using predefined critical actions; completing all critical actions was required to successfully complete the scenario. A generalized linear mixed model with a binomial distribution and logit link function was used for each paramedic pair to estimate the adjusted odds ratio (OR) for successfully completing a scenario with or without the application.

**RESULTS**: Of 112 paramedics, 98 (88%) participated, forming 49 pairs. One pair withdrew before study completion, leaving 48 pairs for analysis. For scenarios using the application, 17/48 (35.4%) successfully completed the scenario compared to 3/48 (6.3%) for scenarios not using the application, adjusted odds 8.28 (95% CI 2.21-31.09). Among scenarios using the application, 10/25 (40%) adult scenarios and 7/23 (30.4%) pediatric scenarios met successful completion criteria compared to 3/23 (13%) adult and 0/25 (0%) pediatric with standard practice alone. User experience survey results demonstrated that participating paramedics assessed the application as being practical to use and valuable for clinical care.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Use of the mobile decision support application improves odds of performing high-quality clinical care in simulated trauma patient scenarios. Further studies are needed to evaluate performance and usability in a field environment.

articles.title: Five-Year Experience with Automated Head Up Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation for Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: Automated head-up position cardiopulmonary resuscitation (AHUP-CPR), the combination of a head and thorax positioning device, active compression-decompression CPR, and an impedance threshold device, lowers intracranial pressure and increases cerebral blood flow and neurologically favorable survival in animal models versus conventional CPR (C-CPR).

**METHODS**: This prospective, observational, investigator-initiated registry study reports 5-year multi-center outcomes after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) from areas served by emergency medical services (EMS) agencies that implemented AHUP-CPR as their routine first-responder standard of care. Adults with non-traumatic OHCA were initially treated with immediate conventional (C-CPR) followed by rapid transition to AHUP-CPR. The primary study focus was on patients who survived to hospital discharge with favorable neurological function (HD-FN). Additional analyses included assessment of sustained return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), survival to hospital discharge (HD), outcomes based upon the presenting rhythm, and impact of covariates on HD-FN.

**RESULTS**: Ten EMS agencies serving 1.5 million people across nine U.S. states contributed data to the AHUP-CPR Registry. A total of 3,709 OHCA patients met enrollment criteria. Across five years, (2020-2024), the average (± SD) interval from 9-1-1 call receipt-to-professional CPR was 9.62 ± 5.78 min. Incidence of ROSC, HD, and HD-FN were 29.5%, 13.1%, and 10.5%, respectively. The incidence of HD-FN for patients presenting with a shockable rhythm meeting Utstein criteria, pulseless electrical activity, or asystole were 33.9%, 11.8%, and 2.0%, respectively. Among 391 neurologically favorable survivors, 91% had a Cerebral Performance Category score of 1 (normal or near normal brain function) at HD. The average age of the survivors was 56.8 ± 16.3 years. Age, interval from 9-1-1 call to professional CPR, witnessed status, and initial rhythm were the most significant predictors of HD-FN using multivariable Poisson regression.

**CONCLUSIONS**: In this 5-year observational registry study, use of AHUP-CPR for the treatment of OHCA was associated with survival to HD of 13.1% and HD-FN of 10.5% in the overall cohort, which comprised patients presenting in shockable rhythms, PEA, and asystole. Drawn from 3,709 OHCA patients treated across diverse EMS systems, these findings provide the largest clinical practice-based characterization to date of the outcomes associated with early transition to AHUP-CPR.

articles.title: Prehospital Resource Utilization After Video-Assisted Versus Telephone-Only Emergency Calls: A Post Hoc Analysis of the CAM-VISION Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: To examine whether video assistance during emergency calls reduced actual prehospital resource utilization across the complete response pathway compared with telephone-only calls.

**METHODS**: This post hoc analysis included 18,745 calls from the cluster-randomized CAM-VISION parent trial (NCT05742412; 8,124 video; 10,621 telephone only). Outcomes were assessed at call level according to telecommunicator allocation and included unit dispatch, pathway progression, number of units, and cumulative unit time. Effects were estimated with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) accounting for clustering by telecommunicator.

**RESULTS**: Initial unit dispatch occurred in 69.4% of video-group calls and 73.9% of telephone-only calls (risk difference, -4.5 percentage points; 95% confidence intervals (CI) (-10.0 to 1.0). Among calls with no unit initially dispatched, subsequent unit dispatch was uncommon (5.1% vs 5.5%). Across the complete response pathway, 71.0% versus 75.3% received at least 1 unit (risk difference, -4.4 percentage points; 95% CI, -9.6 to 0.8), and 69.3% versus 73.8% had a unit reach the scene (risk difference, -4.5 percentage points; 95% CI, -10.0 to 1.0). More than 1 unit was dispatched in 23.3% versus 25.0%. Mean units per call were 1.005 versus 1.054 (mean difference, -0.049; 95% CI, -0.148 to 0.049); mean cumulative unit time was 52.8 versus 54.3 minutes (mean difference, -1.5; 95% CI, -6.2 to 3.1). Overall, differences in initial dispatch were concentrated in ambulance use.

**CONCLUSIONS**: No statistically significant absolute differences in conventional prehospital resource utilization were observed. Point estimates were consistently lower in the video group, primarily through fewer initial dispatches, and subsequent dispatch did not materially offset this numerical difference.

articles.title: Is Social Vulnerability Associated with Discharge Disposition After Trauma Laparotomy?
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Social vulnerability may influence rehabilitation discharge after trauma independent of functional recovery needs. We evaluated whether neighborhood-level social vulnerability was associated with rehabilitation discharge and whether this association persisted when discharge appropriateness was assessed using objective mobility scores.

**STUDY DESIGN**: This retrospective, single-center cohort study included adult trauma laparotomy patients receiving physical therapy from 01/2020-06/2023. Social vulnerability was assessed using the social vulnerability index (SVI) and area deprivation index (ADI). Rehabilitation appropriateness was defined using an Activity Measure for Post-Acute Care (AM-PAC) score ≤16. Primary and secondary outcomes were rehabilitation discharge and mobility-informed rehabilitation appropriateness, respectively. Associations were evaluated using binomial regression adjusted for prespecified covariates.

**RESULTS**: Among 572 patients, 119 (20.8%) were discharged to rehabilitation, and 103 (18%) had AM-PAC scores ≤16. Median SVI was 0.75 and ADI was 63.0. Greater social vulnerability was associated with lower odds of rehabilitation discharge (SVI: aOR 0.17, 95% CI 0.06-0.53, P<0.01), whereas ADI was not (aOR 0.99, 95% CI 0.98-1.00, P=0.21). When accounting for AM-PAC scores, neither SVI (aOR 1.06, 95% CI 0.39-2.88, P=0.91) nor ADI (aOR 0.99, 95% CI 0.99-1.01, P=0.27) was associated with appropriate rehabilitation discharge.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Greater social vulnerability was associated with lower rehabilitation discharge rates after trauma laparotomy, but not with mobility-informed rehabilitation discharge. Incorporating objective mobility assessments into discharge planning may help identify rehabilitation needs while limiting the influence of social factors.

articles.title: Association of Walch glenoid morphology and fracture patterns in proximal humeral fractures.
articles.abstract:
**PURPOSE**: Proximal humeral fracture (PHF) assessment focuses on fracture pattern, bone quality, and patient factors, whereas glenoid morphology-central to biomechanics in glenohumeral arthritis and instability-is overlooked. We hypothesized that glenoid morphology consistent with Walch type B (posterior decentring) is independently associated with complex, tuberculum-involving PHFs.

**METHODS**: This single-centre, retrospective cohort study analysed 919 patients with a PHF and shoulder computed tomography (CT). Two blinded shoulder-subspecialized orthopedic trauma surgeons independently classified all cases; agreement was quantified with Cohen's κ. Fractures were classified by the Neer and AO/OTA systems and glenoid morphology by the Walch classification. The primary outcome-tuberculum involvement (Neer IV/V)-was analysed by multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age at trauma, sex, and osteoarthritis.

**RESULTS**: The cohort comprised 919 patients (72.6% female; median age at trauma 69 years). The Walch distribution in this CT-selected cohort was type A 42.7%, B 54.4%, C 2.7%, and D 0.2%; osteoarthritis was present in 59.5%. Walch agreement was moderate (κ = 0.53), with disagreement concentrated at the A1↔B1 decentring boundary (p < 0.001). Walch type B was independently associated with tuberculum involvement (adjusted OR 2.07, 95% CI 1.56-2.74; adjusted RR 1.30, 95% CI 1.17-1.45; both p < 0.001) and with greater AO/OTA fracture complexity (adjusted ordinal OR 1.60, p < 0.001). Female sex was independently associated with the outcome (adjusted OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.05-1.97, p = 0.023); age and osteoarthritis were not significant.

**CONCLUSION**: In this CT-selected study population, glenoid morphology consistent with Walch type B was independently associated with complex, tuberculum-involving proximal humeral fractures. The association was statistically robust but clinically modest (AUC 0.62), and Walch type B morphology represented one of several correlates of fracture pattern rather than a standalone predictor. Glenoid morphology may therefore be worth recording during CT and fracture-pattern assessment; these hypothesis-generating findings are not sufficient to modify current treatment algorithms, but support the inclusion of glenoid parameters in future risk models and prospective studies.

**LEVEL OF EVIDENCE**: Level III retrospective cohort study prognostic study.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Guided Suprascapular Nerve Block Versus Intravenous Fentanyl for Analgesia in Patients Presenting to the Emergency Department With Traumatic Scapular Fractures.
articles.abstract:
**STUDY OBJECTIVE**: To compare the analgesic efficacy and safety of ultrasound-guided suprascapular nerve block with intravenous fentanyl in patients with traumatic scapular fractures.

**METHODS**: We conducted an open-label randomized controlled pilot trial in the emergency department (ED) of a Level I trauma center in North India. Adults with traumatic scapular fractures and Defense and Veterans Pain Rating Scale scores of 7 and higher, were randomly assigned to ultrasound-guided suprascapular nerve block or intravenous fentanyl (1 μg/kg). Pain scores were assessed at baseline and 30, 60, 120, 240, and 360 minutes. Secondary outcomes included rescue analgesia and adverse events.

**RESULTS**: Sixty patients were randomly assigned to the 2 groups. Median baseline pain score was 10 in both groups. Pain scores were consistently lower with suprascapular nerve block, with median scores of 3 (interquartile [IQR] 2 to 5) versus 7 (IQR 6 to 8) at 30 minutes. Between-group differences were 4 (95% confidence interval [CI], 3 to 4) at 30 and 60 minutes, 2 (95% CI, 2 to 2) at 120 and 240 minutes, and 1 (95% CI, 1 to 2) at 360 minutes. Rescue analgesia was less frequent with suprascapular nerve block (13% versus 79%; risk difference, -66% [95% CI, 47.5 to 85.2]). Drowsiness was more common with fentanyl (12 versus 2 participants); hypotension occurred in 1 fentanyl recipient and paresthesia in 1 suprascapular nerve block recipient.

**CONCLUSION**: In this pilot randomized trial, ultrasound-guided suprascapular nerve block provided greater and sustained pain relief, reduced rescue analgesia, and fewer systemic adverse effects than intravenous fentanyl in adults with traumatic scapular fractures. Larger multicenter trials are needed to confirm these findings and evaluate cumulative opioid use and longer-term outcomes.

articles.title: Trauma undertriage at a University Hospital in North Norway: the need to look beyond mechanism of injury.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Early multidisciplinary management through trauma team activation (TTA) improves outcomes for severely injured patients. Previous studies at the University Hospital of North Norway (UNN) Tromsø conducted in 2006 and 2013, using Injury Severity Score (ISS) ≥ 16 as reference, found high rates of undertriage at 32% and 28% respectively. The aim of this study was to assess the current undertriage at UNN Tromsø using both ISS ≥ 16 and the New Injury Severity Score (NISS) ≥ 16 as reference.

**METHODS**: We retrospectively reviewed trauma patients admitted to UNN Tromsø in 2018 and 2023. The study included all patients met with TTA as well as all severely injured patients that did not receive TTA during the period. Data were obtained from the local trauma registry and electronic medical records. Undertriage was defined as patients with ISS ≥ 16 and no TTA, and NISS ≥ 16 and no TTA.

**RESULTS**: A total of 527 trauma patients were included. Undertriage based on ISS was 15% overall for 2018 and 2023. When NISS ≥ 16 was applied, the undertriage increased to 18% (31/171). A total of 63% of undertriaged patients fulfilled one or more national TTA criteria but was not admitted with TTA. Low-energy falls were the predominant mechanism of injury (73%) among undertriaged patients. A total of 70% of undertriaged patients had single region injuries, and 40% had organ failure.

**CONCLUSIONS**: The undertriage rate at UNN Tromsø was 15% in 2018 and 2023, still exceeding the recommended level of < 5% according to American College of Surgeons-Committee on Trauma. Undertriage appears largely related to the system's non-compliance with trauma criteria, and injuries sustained in low-energy trauma mechanisms. Use of NISS identifies a larger group of potentially undertriaged patients, including more patients with organ failure who may benefit from TTA.
articles.journal: Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med

articles.title: Is it necessary to distally lock all pertrochanteric cephalo-medullary fixation in the geriatric population?
Cost-effectiveness of paramedic-administered prehospital thrombolysis for ST elevation myocardial infarction.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: Guidelines recommend prehospital thrombolysis for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) if trained clinicians can interpret 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) on site. The Queensland Ambulance Service (QAS) has a well-established prehospital reperfusion program under which all paramedics are trained in prehospital STEMI diagnosis on 12-lead ECG and administering thrombolysis in the field to eligible patients. Whilst the clinical benefits of this treatment are proven, its cost-effectiveness remains to be established.

**METHODS**: We developed a decision-analytic microsimulation model to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of paramedic-administered thrombolysis for prehospital STEMI in the state of Queensland, Australia. The comparator was a hypothetical counterfactual group of patients who were clinically eligible for prehospital thrombolysis but received an alternate treatment pathway. The analysis was conducted from a health provider (Queensland Government) perspective. A lifetime time horizon was used. Input values of the acute phase were derived from our prehospital and linked hospital database of all STEMI patients receiving prehospital thrombolysis from QAS paramedics between January 2022 and December 2024. Input values of the long-term phase were obtained from published literature. Cost was expressed in Australian dollars (AUD) and United States dollars (USD) in 2026 value, and effectiveness in quality-adjusted life years (QALYs).

**RESULTS**: Prehospital thrombolysis improved outcomes at a cost of AUD 16,750.22 per QALY gained (95% uncertainty range AUD 15,477.48 - 18,422.84) or USD 11,725.15 (USD 10,834.24 - 12,895.99). In the sensitivity analysis, the cost-effectiveness of prehospital thrombolysis was robust to changes in input values.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Paramedic-administered thrombolysis in the field for prehospital STEMI, compared with no such treatment, represents value for money.

articles.title: A Lighter Approach to Language Access: Virtual Interpreter Utilization in Emergency Medical Services (EMS).
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: Limited English Proficiency (LEP) may create communication barriers during prehospital care. Although on-demand interpreter services are often available to emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians, utilization may be limited by device accessibility, workflow barriers, and clinician adoption. Our objective was to evaluate whether implementation of agency-issued lightweight clinician-carried smartphones was associated with increased utilization of virtual interpreter services during prehospital care.

**METHODS**: We conducted an observational retrospective pre-post cohort study of virtual interpreter service utilization within a large multistate Midwest EMS agency. On June 1, 2025, the agency issued smartphones (Apple iPhone 16, ∼6 ounces) to all clinicians, providing continuous access to virtual audio and video interpreter services (LanguageLine Solutions). Previously, interpreter services were accessed using large Toughbook laptops (∼6.1 pounds). Interpreter utilization was compared between pre-implementation (October 30, 2024, to May 31, 2025) and post-implementation (June 1, 2025, to December 31, 2025) periods. Interpreter requests per 100 encounters were compared using rate ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

**RESULTS**: Interpreter requests increased from 104 pre-implementation (0.19 per 100 encounters, 95% CI: 0.15-0.23) to 326 post-implementation (0.57 per 100 encounters, 95% CI: 0.51-0.63; RR= 3.04, 95% CI: 2.44-3.79; p < 0.001). Audio requests increased from 68 calls (0.12 per 100 encounters) to 271 calls (0.47 per 100 encounters; RR = 3.86, 95% CI: 2.96-5.03; p < 0.001). Video requests increased from 36 calls (0.06 per 100 encounters) to 55 calls (0.10 per 100 encounters), although the observed increase did not reach statistical significance (RR= 1.48, 95% CI: 0.97-2.25; p = 0.066). The most commonly requested languages were Spanish (n = 153, 36%), Somali (n = 146, 34%), and Arabic (n = 41, 10%).

**CONCLUSIONS**: Implementation of agency-issued lightweight clinician-carried smartphones was associated with a threefold increase in virtual interpreter utilization. This increase was driven primarily by audio interpretation, while the observed increase in video utilization did not reach statistical significance. These findings suggest that improving point-of-care accessibility of interpreter services through lightweight mobile devices may facilitate greater utilization during prehospital encounters with patients with LEP.

articles.title: Research on the morphology and injury mechanism of pilon fractures.
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: Understanding the relationship between injury mechanisms and fracture morphology in high-energy Pilon fractures is essential for optimizing preoperative planning and surgical outcomes. To investigate the associations between injury mechanisms and fracture morphology in high-energy Pilon fractures and to provide a theoretical basis for precision diagnosis and treatment.

**METHODS**: This retrospective study included 192 patients with high-energy Pilon fractures treated at Lianyungang Second People's Hospital between January 2010 and December 2024. Using a standardized "trauma history-first plus imaging cross-validation" protocol, patients were categorized into 5 groups: dorsiflexion, varus, valgus, plantarflexion, and neutral. Two senior orthopedic surgeons (≥ 10 years of experience) independently and blindly assessed anteroposterior and lateral tibiofibular radiographs, CT scans, and three-dimensional reconstructions. Evaluated parameters included fibular fracture level and type, tibial fragment distribution, fracture angle, and Topliss classification. Interobserver reliability was assessed using Cohen's kappa coefficient. Group comparisons were performed using the chi-square (χ²) test or Fisher's exact test with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons. Statistical significance was defined as P < 0.05.

**RESULTS**: Among the 192 patients, 154 (80.2%) were male and 38 (19.8%) were female. The mean (SD) age was 43.38 (12.56) years (range, 14-71 years). Interobserver agreement was substantial for injury mechanism classification (κ = 0.82; 95% CI, 0.75-0.89) and core morphological assessments (κ = 0.87; 95% CI, 0.81-0.93). Fracture morphology differed significantly among mechanism groups (P < 0.05). Dorsiflexion injuries were characterized by the "medial + anterolateral + Die-punch" fragment pattern (45.0%; 95% CI, 23.1%-66.9%), fracture angles > 90° (65.0%), and coronal Y-shaped fractures (25.0%). Varus injuries predominantly showed the "anterolateral + posterolateral + medial + Die-punch" pattern (32.5%) and simple sagittal split fractures (40.0%). Valgus injuries were associated with comminuted fibular fractures (64.3%) and coronal V/Y-shaped tibial fractures (35.7%). Plantarflexion injuries typically involved posterolateral fragments (61.5%) and fracture angles > 90° (80.8%). Neutral injuries were characterized by complex multifragmentary comminuted fractures with Die-punch collapse (33.7%).

**CONCLUSION**: There is a significant and reproducible association between injury mechanisms and fracture morphology in high-energy Pilon fractures. This mechanism-based morphological characterization may provide an objective reference for preoperative assessment and individualized surgical planning. The clinical utility and prognostic value of this classification framework still need to be verified in further prospective studies with clinical outcome endpoints.

articles.title: Critically ill trauma in Portugal: a multicenter intensive care cohort study of frailty, organ dysfunction, and outcomes.
articles.abstract:
**PURPOSE**: Multicenter data on critically ill trauma patients admitted to Portuguese intensive care units (ICUs) are lacking. We aimed to characterize their epidemiology, injury profile, organ dysfunction trajectories and outcomes, and to evaluate the prognostic performance of severity and frailty measures.

**METHODS**: Multicenter retrospective cohort study within the National Intensive Care Registry (RNMI) of adults (≥ 18 years) admitted to an ICU as a direct consequence of trauma (1 October-31 December 2024) in 32 of 50 voluntarily participating Portuguese ICUs; not nationally representative. SAPS II, ISS, TRISS, the Clinical Frailty Scale, daily SOFA scores, organ support, quality of life and mortality were collected. Prognostic performance was assessed by ROC analysis, multivariable logistic regression, calibration, and mixed-effects modelling of serial SOFA.

**RESULTS**: 457 patients were included; median age 61 years (IQR 45-74), 72.0% male. Falls were the leading injury mechanism (46.9%). Traumatic brain injury (32.9%) and thoracic trauma (21.4%) predominated. Observed ICU and hospital mortality were 11.0% and 15.3%, respectively. SOFA scores were consistently higher in non-survivors from day one. SAPS II showed the highest discrimination for hospital mortality (AUC 0.874, 95% CI 0.825-0.924), followed by TRISS (0.758) and the Clinical Frailty Scale (0.702). SAPS II, day-1 SOFA, and frailty were independently associated with hospital mortality. SAPS II over-predicted mortality (observed/expected 0.64), whereas TRISS showed a non-significant tendency to under-predict it (1.32, 95% CI 0.99-1.72).

**CONCLUSIONS**: In this multicenter cohort from 32 voluntarily participating ICUs, patients were older, with frequent falls, neurotrauma and thoracic injury, and moderate mortality. Organ dysfunction trajectories and frailty were associated with hospital mortality, but incremental predictive value was not assessed; both merit inclusion in future trauma registry frameworks.

articles.title: Influence of cerebrospinal fluid dynamics on aseptic bone flap resorption: a single-center retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVE**: Aseptic bone flap resorption (ABFR) remains a common complication after autologous cranioplasty following decompressive craniectomy (DC), with reported prevalences varying widely-often reported between 10% and 30%-likely due to inconsistent follow-up. Data on cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics in pathogenesis of ABFR are scarce. Aim of the present study was therefore to identify potential risk factors, with a particular focus on CSF drainage procedures.

**METHODS**: In this retrospective single-center study, we reviewed consecutive patients who underwent DC followed by autologous cranioplasty from 2015 to 2022. We collected demographics, clinical details, perioperative variables, and CSF interventions. Univariate and multivariate analyses identified associations, with subgroup focus on patients completing structured follow-up.

**RESULTS**: ABFR was diagnosed in 39/259 patients (15.1%), resulting in 38/101 (37.6%) in the 6-months follow-up cohort. Changes in CSF dynamics such as preoperative lumbar CSF drainage (p = 0.035) were identified as a risk factor, whereas ventriculoperitoneal shunt pressure adjustment was not associated with an increased risk of ABFR. After differentiation of the direction of adjustment, pressure reduction was not associated with ABFR. Especially preoperative lumbar CSF drainage remains an independent risk factor (p = 0.023) in multivariate analysis.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Without structured imaging follow-up, ABFR rates are likely underestimated. CSF dynamic alterations beyond shunt presence alone may represent a relevant risk factor for ABFR. Our findings emphasize that primary alloplastic cranioplasty could be considered in at least a subgroup of patients.

articles.title: Trauma-associated cardiac arrest - insights and results from a German rescue helicopter station.
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: In comparison with cardiac arrest attributable to other causes, trauma-associated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest has low survival rates, but survivors often show good neurological recovery. This study aimed to provide a deeper understanding of trauma-associated cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) in terms of trauma mechanisms, injury patterns, CPR measures, and outcomes.

**METHODS**: In this retrospective single-center study, emergency physician reports on trauma-associated CPRs performed by the Christoph 22 helicopter emergency medical service (HEMS) from 2013 to 2023 at the study site in Ulm were analyzed using the chi-square test and binary logistic regression.

**RESULTS**: In total, 126 cases of prehospital trauma-associated CPR at the Ulm HEMS site were included. Four patients (3.2%) survived, with all four showing good neurological recovery. The most common cause of trauma was motorcycle accident. The patients most frequently presented with traumatic brain injury (TBI) (69.6%) and/or chest injuries (79.2%). Chest decompression was performed in 93.9% of the patients with chest injuries. TBI was the only injury to show a (negative) association with 30-day survival (1.1% vs. 7.9%; p = 0.049), this observation was independent of whether the TBI was isolated or occurred in combination with pelvic, abdominal, and/or chest injuries.

**CONCLUSION**: In this study on trauma-associated CPR, the survival rate remained low, but the neurological recovery of survivors was often good. TBI, both isolated and in combination with chest, abdomen, and/or pelvic injuries, seemed to be a prognostically unfavorable factor. However, with only four long-term survivors, it is hardly possible to draw reliable conclusions.

articles.title: Carboxypeptidase B1: A novel, targetable contributor to thromboembolic complications in severe acute pancreatitis?
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) is associated with increased thrombotic risk. Systemic release of pancreatic proteases in SAP may alter susceptibility to endogenous fibrinolysis, but this remains unexplored. Pancreatic carboxypeptidase B1 (CPB1) is a protease activated by trypsin that shares cleavage specificity with thrombin-activatable fibrinolysis inhibitor, which cleaves C-terminal lysine residues off fibrin, impairing co-localization of tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) and plasminogen and rendering clots resistant to fibrinolysis. We hypothesized that circulating CPB1 would be elevated in SAP patients and contribute to fibrinolytic resistance.

**METHODS**: Plasma and clinical data were prospectively collected from SAP patients (n=15), matched critically ill controls without pancreatitis (n=13), and healthy controls (n=4) with IRB approval and informed consent. CPB1 levels were measured through ELISA. Clot lysis assays assessed fibrinolysis in response to tPA. Healthy control plasma was tested with and without porcine pancreas CPB1 to assess the effect of CPB1 on fibrinolysis. Transition midpoints (TM's) were defined as the time to 50% clot lysis. Clinical data were analyzed using Mann-Whitney U and Fisher exact tests. Assay results were analyzed using Kruskall-Wallis test. Significance was set at P<0.05.

**RESULTS**: Demographics were similar between groups. SAP patients had markedly elevated CPB1 levels (154.0 [58.4-388.0] ng/mL) compared with sick (7.0 [4.1-15.6] ng/mL, P<0.0001) and healthy controls (4.0 [2.1-4.4], P<0.001). Healthy control plasma supplemented with porcine pancreas CPB1 demonstrated complete disruption of fibrinolysis compared with healthy plasma without CPB1. SAP patients had the highest resistance to tPA-induced fibrinolysis, with significantly higher baseline TMs than critically ill controls (42.0 [21.7-126.6] vs. 22.8 [18.3-33.7], P=0.04).

**CONCLUSIONS**: Patients with SAP have uniquely elevated circulating levels of CPB1, which may contribute to thromboembolism in SAP through fibrinolytic resistance. Further investigation into targeted CPB1 inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy in SAP is warranted to potentially reduce development of organ failure and mortality.

**LEVEL OF EVIDENCE**: N/A (Basic Science).

articles.title: Fluid eMTBR-tau243 as a Biomarker of Mixed 3-Repeat and 4-Repeat Tau Pathology.
articles.abstract:
**IMPORTANCE**: Neurodegenerative diseases with abnormal tau protein aggregation in the brain (ie, tauopathies) can be classified by the tau isoform that accumulates: 3-repeat (3R), 4-repeat (4R), or mixed 3R/4R tauopathies, which include chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), some forms of frontotemporal lobar degeneration, and Alzheimer disease (AD). The endogenously cleaved form of tau microtubule binding region containing the residue 243 (eMTBR-tau243) can be detected in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and blood and has been associated with AD tau pathology, but its specificity and biological interpretation in non-AD tauopathies remains unclear.

**OBJECTIVE**: To evaluate biofluid eMTBR-tau243 in a range of tauopathies.

**DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS**: This case-control study included 4 biorepositories based in the US that contributed CSF and plasma samples from participants with and without tauopathies, many of whom had antemortem biofluid samples paired with autopsy or genetically defined neuropathology. Samples were analyzed between August 2023 and December 2025. Data analysis occurred from August 2024 to July 2026.

**EXPOSURE**: CSF and plasma eMTBR-tau243 concentrations measured using a mass spectrometry-based assay.

**MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES**: Outcomes included mixed 3R/4R tauopathy (eg, AD and CTE) based on autopsy, frontotemporal lobar degeneration with MAPT variants (FTLD-MAPT), and CTE stage. Differences in biomarker levels between groups were evaluated using analysis of variance or analysis of covariance, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was calculated to evaluate the discriminative performance of fluid eMTBR-tau243.

**RESULTS**: Among the 229 participants (196 with CSF samples and 55 with plasma samples [22 with both]), mean (SD) age at fluid sample collection was 63 (13) years and 108 (47%) were female. Median (IQR) CSF eMTBR-tau243 was increased in 10 patients with AD (0.459 [0.246-0.801] fmol/mL) compared with 29 cognitively unimpaired controls (0.002 [0.001-0.005] fmol/mL) (adjusted P < .001), but other autopsy-confirmed non-AD tauopathies (which included 52 individuals with conditions including progressive supranuclear palsy and corticobasal degeneration) did not demonstrate an increase (0.015 [0.008, 0.039] fmol/mL). Six symptomatic FTLD-MAPT variant carriers with mixed 3R/4R tauopathy (R406W, V337M, and G389R) had increased median (IQR) CSF eMTBR-tau243 (0.140 [0.055-0.174] fmol/mL) compared with 15 4R tauopathy variant carriers including N279K and P301L (0.004 [0.001-0.044] fmol/mL) (P = .001). Median (IQR) plasma eMTBR-tau243 was increased in 11 patients with CTE (1.93 [0.42-3.68] fmol/L) compared with 20 cognitively unimpaired controls (0.29 [0.05-0.62] fmol/L) (adjusted P = .007), but did not increase as high as among 14 patients with AD (11.25 [2.29-19.38] fmol/L). Plasma eMTBR-tau243 distinguished CTE stage III and IV from controls (AUC, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.92-1.00), but not CTE stage I from controls (AUC, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.32-0.97).

**CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE**: This study found that plasma and CSF eMTBR-tau243 were increased in mixed 3R/4R tauopathies including AD, high-stage CTE, and a subset of genetic FTLD-MAPT, compared with cognitively unimpaired controls. Further validation in larger cohorts is needed to determine the clinical utility of eMTBR-tau243 as a potential diagnostic biomarker for CTE and other tauopathies beyond AD.

articles.title: Impact of antibiotic prophylaxis on the occurrence of early-onset ventilator-associated pneumonia in trauma patients (antiVAP): a propensity score-weighted, retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Short-course antibiotic prophylaxis has been associated with a reduced risk of early-onset ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) in selected populations, particularly patients with acute brain injury. However, its role in severely injured trauma patients remains controversial.

**METHODS**: This multicentre, retrospective cohort study, conducted in 15 French trauma centres, included severely injured adults who required mechanical ventilation initiated within 24 h of admission and continued for at least 48 h. Propensity score-based analyses assessed the association between early antibiotic prophylaxis (initiated within the first 24 h of management and continued for up to 72 h) and patient outcomes. The primary outcome was early-onset VAP; secondary outcomes included late-onset VAP, extrapulmonary infections, duration of mechanical ventilation, ICU and hospital length of stay, and 30-day mortality.

**RESULTS**: A total of 1,321 trauma patients were included. Antibiotic prophylaxis was administered to 746 patients (56%), with amoxicillin-clavulanic acid used in more than 90% of cases. Early-onset VAP occurred in 240 of 746 patients (32%) who received antibiotic prophylaxis and in 195 of 575 (34%) who did not. After inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), antibiotic prophylaxis was not associated with early-onset VAP (weighted odds ratio [wOR] 0.87, 95% CI 0.66-1.22; p = 0.48). A cause-specific Cox model accounting for the competing risk of death before day 7 yielded similar results (cause-specific hazard ratio [csHR] 0.87, 95% CI 0.71-1.07; p = 0.19). Antibiotic prophylaxis was not associated with improve of secondary outcomes.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Routine antibiotic prophylaxis in severely injured trauma patients was not associated with a reduced risk of early-onset VAP.

**CLINICALTRIALS**: Gov ID NCT07059039 - Registration date: July, 10th 2025.

articles.title: Acute kidney injury and renal replacement therapy: a critical synthesis of metabolic derangements and nutritional implications.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Acute kidney injury (AKI) affects up to 50% of critically ill patients and is frequently complicated by severe metabolic derangements, requiring the initiation of replacement therapy (RRT) in 10-15% of cases. Despite substantial progress in the diagnosis of AKI and optimisation of RRT delivery, the nutritional management of these patients remains an underexplored area.

**MAIN BODY**: AKI is increasingly recognised as a systemic metabolic disorder extending beyond impaired renal clearance. Key metabolic alterations include mitochondrial dysfunction, dysregulated gluconeogenesis, increased proteolysis and altered amino acid metabolism, with accelerated nitrogen wasting. These abnormalities are further amplified by acute systemic stress states, including sepsis, systemic inflammation, trauma, burns, liver dysfunction and multiorgan failure. RRT introduces additional metabolic consequences through extracorporeal losses of amino acids and micronutrients. Conversely, citrate anticoagulation, glucose-containing dialysate, and lactate-buffered solutions represent sources of clinically relevant calories.
